question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable exec approval timeout, and if so what canonical key, bounds, and precedence should it use?
rationale: The requested knob controls the authorization window for host command execution and adds public config surface, which repository policy treats as security- and upgrade-sensitive.

options.title: Add a bounded canonical config key
options.body: Define one supported key, validation bounds, default, docs, and tests before any implementation PR lands.

options.title: Keep the fixed default
options.body: Leave the 30-minute timeout hardcoded and rely on fail-fast fixes for surfaces where approval can never be delivered.

options.title: Fold into broader exec policy design
options.body: Track timeout tuning with other exec approval policy changes instead of landing a standalone knob now.

recommendation.title: Add a bounded canonical config key
recommendation.body: Define one supported key, validation bounds, default, docs, and tests before any implementation PR lands.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the central timeout behavior and is the clearest history-backed owner for deciding whether this security boundary should become config.
